title: Continuous Wearage
description: User continuously wears the device, providing constant access to sensor data.
assumptions: User is aware of the device and intends to wear it continuously.

title: Continuous Data Capture
description: Device continuously captures sensor telemetry (heart rate, step counts, GPS, timestamps) from the wearer.
assumptions: Device is functioning correctly and has access to the wearer's biometric data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Transfer of personal data (exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, timestamps) from the Wearable Device (Process P1) to the Companion Mobile App (Process P2) constitutes a data disclosure. This is an explicit disclosure of personal data across a boundary, as the device is transferring sensitive user data to a third-party application.
assumptions: The data transferred is considered personal data based on the context of 'exercise sessions, GPS traces, device id, timestamps' being sensitive user information.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (Process P2) is receiving and processing personal data from the Wearable Device (Process P1). This represents a data disclosure where the app is acting as a data receiver and processor of the transferred data.
assumptions: The app is processing the data in a manner that could be considered disclosure to the user or for user-specific purposes.

title: Unawareness as a user sharing personal data
description: The user (ExternalEntity EE1) does not need to be the data subject for the data to be processed. The user is merely a conduit for the data to be entered into the Companion Mobile App (Process P2).
assumptions: The user is not the data subject.

title: Unawareness as a process sharing personal data
description: The Companion Mobile App (Process P2) does not need to be the data subject for the data to be processed. The app is merely a conduit for the data to be entered by the user.
assumptions: The app is not the data subject.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) writes health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) to the Health Log Store (DS1). This constitutes a data disclosure as the app transfers personal health data to a third-party data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Log Store (DS1) receives health logs from the Companion Mobile App (P2). This represents a data disclosure where the store is the recipient of personal health data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the Location History Store (DS2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the app transfers personal data (location traces) to a third-party data store.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Location History Store (DS2) receives data from the Companion Mobile App (P2). This is a data disclosure as the store receives personal data from a third-party process.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Health Log Store (DS1) transfers personal health data (calories, weight, exercise logs) to the Health Analytics Service (P3) for processing. This constitutes a data disclosure as the store is transferring data across a boundary to a third party (the analytics service) for health-condition analysis.
assumptions: The data transfer is intended and designed for the analytics service to process the logs.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Health Analytics Service (P3) receives and processes personal health data from the Health Log Store (DS1). This involves the transfer of personal data across a boundary to the store for analysis.
assumptions: The service is processing the logs as intended for health-condition analysis.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) queries the Location History Store (DS2) to derive daily routine and movement patterns. This interaction involves the transfer of personal location data from the data store to the analytics process, which may constitute a data disclosure if the data is considered personal and the transfer is not strictly necessary for the service's core functionality.
assumptions: The data retrieved from DS2 is personal location history.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the specific data retrieved is strictly required for the derived patterns or if the service could use aggregated, anonymized, or non-personal data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) processes location data from the Location History Store (DS2) to derive daily routine and movement patterns. This process may involve the transfer of personal location data to an external entity (the analytics service itself or a downstream system) for pattern analysis, which could be considered a data disclosure.
assumptions: The derived patterns rely on the personal location data from DS2.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the derived patterns are considered personal data or if the service could use aggregated, anonymized, or non-personal data.

title: Profiling a group of individuals
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) processes health-condition risk indicators and trend flags to generate insights about a larger group of individuals. This constitutes a Linking threat where data of a single individual leads to insights about a larger group of individuals, potentially violating privacy principles regarding the aggregation of personal data.
assumptions: The analytics service aggregates individual health indicators to produce group-level insights.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) discloses inferred insights (health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) to the Companion Mobile App (P2). This represents a Data Disclosure threat where personal health data is transmitted to an external entity without appropriate consent or security controls.
assumptions: The app is an external entity receiving the analytics data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Companion Mobile App (P2) receives and processes health-condition risk indicators and trend flags from the Health Analytics Service (P3). This represents a Data Disclosure threat where personal health data is transmitted from an external entity to another.
assumptions: The app is an external entity receiving the analytics data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The companion mobile app (Process P2) is transmitting user data (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) to an external entity (User/EE1). This constitutes a data disclosure risk as the process is exposing sensitive health information to an external system.
assumptions: The app is actively displaying trends and inferred condition indicators to the user.

title: Identifying
description: The user (ExternalEntity EE1) is being identified as the recipient of health-related data from the app. This represents a privacy risk where the user's identity is being linked to their health status.
assumptions: The app is displaying trends and inferred condition indicators to the user.

title: Data Disclosure to Cloud Hosting Provider
description: The Health Analytics Service (P3) transfers analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset to the Cloud Hosting Provider (EE2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system is transferring personal data to a third party.

title: Data Disclosure to Health Analytics Service
description: The Cloud Hosting Provider (EE2) transfers the hosted and replicated analytics data, models, and health/location datasets to the Health Analytics Service (P3). This constitutes a data disclosure as the system is transferring personal data to a third party.
